scope: Opened development checkpoint; generic-instruction adoption study with a same-model, same-ceiling ordinary Code control added after observing Hegel. Exploratory comparison, not a preregistered or held-out superiority trial.
change: Only STRATEGIES[hegel] now asks for explanations with conditions and predictions across experiments, revised using paid evidence. Existing notes, tools, selector, execution and parent scheduling are retained.
previous_strategy: Organize research around explicit revisable hypotheses. When a parent's experiment depends on an uncertain instrument, representation or condition, open that child question, acquire evidence, and return an executable analysis to the parent. Let the answer change the next experiment. Retain useful procedures with their applicability conditions; reopen unsupported dependencies when evidence changes. For a measured numerical relation, use the research operator to bind public readings and executable experiments to hypothesis search; consume its returned child answer in the parent program. Revise the binding when it reports ambiguity or failed validation. For exploration without such a relation, ordinary world actions remain available.
current_strategy: Organize research around revisable explanations of the question you are resolving. Retain their applicability conditions and implications across experiments in research_notes. Use paid evidence to revise those explanations within the scope actually tested. A prediction that one finite experiment succeeds or fails answers that experiment; also consider what it establishes about the parent explanation. For a further experiment, compare what the surviving explanations predict under its conditions, using the existing research or contrast tools when applicable. Choose among executable experiments on that basis. If current observations cannot distinguish the explanations, state what remains unobservable and investigate a measurement or representation that could distinguish them. If you cannot yet justify competing explanations or distinct predictions, record that limitation and choose exploratory work; do not invent alternatives merely to fill a design. When a parent's experiment depends on an uncertain instrument, representation or condition, open that child question, acquire evidence, and return an executable analysis to the parent. Let the answer change the next experiment. Retain useful procedures with their applicability conditions; reopen unsupported dependencies when evidence changes. For a measured numerical relation, use the research operator to bind public readings and executable experiments to hypothesis search; consume its returned child answer in the parent program. Revise the binding when it reports ambiguity or failed validation. For exploration without such a relation, ordinary world actions remain available.
authorship: The host changes a generic research requirement. The runtime model authors all scientific hypotheses, variable choices, experiments, predictions, programs and analyses. No mid-run scientific hints or source edits.
outcomes: Read authored explanations, proposed alternative experiments, actual predicted and observed outcomes, subsequent revision, parent changes and task completion. Do not infer adoption from field counts or number of calls.
limit_rationale: Allow formation, execution and revision under a 64-call cumulative ceiling; the previous 32-call treatment ended at its ceiling. All inherited and new costs remain separate. Different limits preclude treating previous outcomes as a matched performance baseline.

control_extension.scope: Exploratory same-model, same-ceiling Code control added after observing ongoing Hegel scanning. This is not a preregistered or held-out superiority trial.
control_extension.common_controls: Same source question, full paid observation prefix, all scientific files and notes, existing tools, model, shared cumulative cost accounting and limits.
control_extension.difference: Existing code_archive strategy and absence of Hegel-specific automatic research focus; voluntary inquiry and all research operators remain available.
